title: Verify a webhook signature over its original bytes
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/api/webhooks/route.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode: export async function POST(request:Request){const json=await request.json();await processEvent(json);return Response.json({ok:true});}

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Use the provider SDK/test vector to verify exact body bytes.
Reject changed bytes, invalid signatures and out-of-window timestamps.
Deliver the same event concurrently and crash between receipt and business mutation.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: Parsing and reserializing JSON can change the signed byte sequence.

alternativeApproaches: Only if a durable queue/outbox has accepted responsibility. A process-local promise after returning 200 can lose the event on shutdown; a provider may stop retrying after that acknowledgement.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
